disguise

/dis-GHYZE/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Disguise means to change one's appearance or behavior in order to conceal one's true identity or nature.

The prince disguised himself as a beggar so he could walk through the market unrecognized.

Worked Example

To research how staff actually treated customers, the restaurant's owner disguised herself with a wig, glasses, and an unfamiliar accent before sitting down for an ordinary lunch service, gathering an honest picture that no announced inspection ever could have.

The owner didn't just dress up for fun — she deliberately hid her real identity to get an unfiltered, honest experience, which is exactly what "disguise" means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

conceal: Conceal means to hide something from view or knowledge — you conceal an object behind a crate or a feeling behind a smile. Disguise is more specific and more active: it changes appearance so a thing stays in plain sight but goes unrecognized. Concealed things aren't seen; disguised things are seen and misread.

impersonate: Impersonate means to pass yourself off as one specific other person — an officer, a celebrity. Disguise only requires hiding who you are; you can disguise yourself as a generic stranger without claiming anyone's identity. Every impersonation involves disguise, but not every disguise impersonates.

veil: Veil means to cover something so it is only partly seen — mist veils a mountain; a diplomat veils a threat in polite words. Disguise goes further: not a soft covering but a false appearance, built so the true identity underneath is missed entirely.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

reveal: to make something visible or known, the opposite of hiding it

expose: to uncover something that was deliberately hidden

Where it sits · how much of it is concealed — mask → disguise → camouflage

mask vs. disguise: To mask something is to cover just one part or quality, like masking a smell — narrower than a disguise, which changes the whole identity.

camouflage vs. disguise: To camouflage something is to make it blend into its surroundings so well it becomes hard to see at all — while a disguise leaves you in plain view, just unrecognized.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart, away, reversal

Root — guise

Root — guise: manner, style, appearance (Old French guise)

Put it together

Put it together: "disguise" combines dis- with the Old French guise, "manner or appearance" — literally, to turn away from one's usual manner or appearance in order to look like someone or something else.

Use the root in a new word: guise

Use the root in a new word: guise: The con artist operated for years under the guise of a licensed financial advisor.

Word Choice

neutral, playful or serious

Disguise ranges from playful (a child's Halloween costume) to serious (a spy's false identity). It always involves an intentional change meant to prevent recognition.
